questions.question: How should the kernel's proxy collect an unsized read() (BUG-331's _read_whole)? Measured at 256 MiB: list+join 2.00x peak / 151 ms, BytesIO (current) 1.80x / 704 ms, native read() 1.00x / 69 ms.

options.label: List + join (Recommended)
options.description: Revert to the join: about 4.6x faster than BytesIO for 10% more peak memory. The docstring states the 2x peak, and the round-1 tracemalloc test is replaced by one that pins sized reads, not memory. Only custom drivers reading content in full take this path; built-in drivers read in sized chunks.

options.label: Keep BytesIO
options.description: Keep the 1.80x peak and document the time cost (about 4.6x the join's) in the docstring. No code change.

options.label: Size up front
options.description: When the stream exposes a size (fileno + fstat, or seek/tell), read into a preallocated buffer, and fall back to the join otherwise. Closer to native memory for files, but more code and more cells to test in this PR.
